message.content:
The number of distinct positions that can arise in a standard game of chess is astronomically large.  In fact, the famous “Shannon number” – an estimate of the size of the game tree – is on the order of  

\[
N \approx 10^{43}\text{–}10^{46}
\]

So, roughly speaking, there are about **one hundred trillion trillion trillion** (10^43) to **ten hundred trillion trillion trillion** (10^46) different ways the pieces can be arranged on the board during a legal game.  This figure includes all possible permutations of the 32 pieces (king, queen, rooks, bishops, knights, pawns) and the various rules that constrain them (castling rights, en‑passant possibilities, etc.).
